title: Uniform approximation by signed Fourier samples
statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer and let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be nonzero. Write $\widehat f(S)$ for the Fourier–Walsh coefficient at $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and set $L=\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}}|\widehat f(S)|$. For $\delta>0$ and a nonnegative integer $s$ with $4nL^2/\delta^2\le s$, there exist subsets $T_1,\ldots,T_s\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, with repetitions allowed, such that for every $x\in\{0,1\}^n$, $\left|f(x)-\sum_{j=1}^s \frac{L}{s}\operatorname{sgn}_+(\widehat f(T_j))\chi_{T_j}(x)\right|<\delta$, where $\operatorname{sgn}_+(t)=1$ for $t\ge0$ and $-1$ for $t<0$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a nonzero real-valued function on the Boolean cube
$4nL^2/\delta^2\le s$, where $L$ is the sum of the absolute Fourier–Walsh coefficients of $f$
replaced: Let $n\ge0$ and give $\{0,1\}^n$ uniform probability; write $\mathbb E$ for expectation. Put $\chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}(-1)^{x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\mathbb E[h\chi_S]$ for $S\subseteq[n]$ and real cube functions $h$. Write $\operatorname{sgn}_+(t)=1$ for $t\ge0$ and $-1$ for $t<0$. Let $n>0$, let $f$ be a real cube function not identically zero, put $L=\sum_S|\widehat f(S)|$, and let $\delta>0$ and an integer $s\ge0$ satisfy $4nL^2/\delta^2\le s$. There exists a sequence of subsets $T_1,\ldots,T_s\subseteq[n]$, with repetitions allowed, such that $|f(x)-(L/s)\sum_{j=1}^s\operatorname{sgn}_+(\widehat f(T_j))\chi_{T_j}(x)|<\delta$ for every $x\in\{0,1\}^n$.
